answer: According to official vegan certification standards (such as Vegan.org) and FDA labeling guidelines, honey is an animal-derived food product produced by bees. The product artwork explicitly displays the 'Certified Vegan' certification mark on the front panel while the ingredient list specifies 'Honey (1%)' (and 'Honey (9%)' in the formulation sheet). Because vegan standards prohibit all animal-derived ingredients, the packaging cannot claim 'Certified Vegan' while containing honey.
